notes.title: Update 0.6.2 - Restocking, Balance, Quality-of-Life
notes.content:
Salve, amici! Having recently presented at Boston's Festival of Independent Games, I returned to my workshop to hammer out some tweaks to make the game just a smidge better.

[h1]Changes[/h1]
[h2]Shop Restocking & Destocking[/h2]
The shop stock now dynamically restocks. Items also come off of the market each week to represent other buyers. While it's a nice way to make the game feel more alive and make rare equipment more scarce, it's really preparation for Patch 0.7, which will introduce travel.

In 0.7, each city's stores will carry different equipment at different frequencies and the number of goods on offer will be proportional to the city's size. All of that nice systems logic is now there, under the hood, so that we can sail smoothly in to sailing smoothly around the Mediterranean.

[h2]Balance[/h2]
[list]
[*] Injured gladiators now sell at a discount. No more buying a recruit, throwing them into an easy match and selling them right after!
[*] Matches overall are slightly easier, especially 2 skull matches. Previously the step from 1 to 2 was a bit harsh for new players.
[*] A 1 skull challenge will now always be available until the player has won their first match. In addition, the challenge system now loosely tracks your successes, making more higher-difficulty challenges available as you win more (and more difficult) matches.
[/list]

[h2]Quality of Life[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added a button to unequip all items from a gladiator in outfitting
[*] Added a button to return from team select directly to challenge selection
[*] Made the last selected gladiator 'stick' in the outfitting screen when moving back and forth between menus
[*] Increased tooltip font size (and fixed a typo in one of the perk tooltips)
[*] Rearranged outfitting a bit to keep the funds in the same top-right location they normally appear in. Previously they moved to the center of the screen, which was unpleasantly inconsistent
[/list]

[h1]What's Next?[/h1]
The next big patch will take your school on the roads (or, more often, the seas). Equipment and arenas will be more tied to the local culture and size of the city you're in. The markets in big cities will have more on offer and the best equipment will only be available from specific towns with master artisans. Challenges and recruits will eventually reflect the location more as well.

Challenges will only replenish at a certain rate, encouraging you to get out of town and see the world when either you're out of challenges or all your gladiators need time to recover. Travel will cost some time and money, but staying put will still have you paying for your gladiators' upkeep, encouraging you to go find appropriate matches.

All this travel will require a splashy and beautiful new world map as well!

I'm not sure how long this patch will take. It depends a lot on how much I 'front-load' the content of all these locations before release vs just build a skeleton travel system with content to follow.

Either way, I'm really excited to bring the world to life and I hope you will be too!

notes.title: Update 0.6.1 - Balance & Typos
notes.content:
Salve! Just dropping a couple small tweaks to 0.6 based on some additional testing and feedback

[h1]Changes[/h1]
[h2]Balance[/h2]
[list]
[*] Power is less powerful, granting +1% damage per level instead of +2%. This should lead to fewer instances where a gladiator is dispatched in just a couple successful hits.
[*] The final fight of the demo is a bit easier to make it a tractable challenge after 30-odd rounds of prep
[/list]

[h2]Legibility[/h2]
[list]
[*] Enlarged the elements of the training UI. Since you'll likely only have 3-6 gladiators in the demo, there was no need to cram 9 into a single page at the cost of readability
[*] Fixed some typos in tooltips. No longer will you suffer "rgladiators"
[/list]

notes.title: Update 0.6.0 - STATS! (and training)
notes.content:
Salve, dear players!

I'm thrilled to announce patch 0.6.0 just in time for the holidays! The biggest patch just occurred in my own life: I got [i]married[/i] since the last update! In that spirit, I hope [i]you[/i] will fall in love with your new starting gladiators, Dacius, Leander, and Pio. But more on that below.

[h1]What's New in 0.6.0[/h1]
[h2]Major Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Stats[/b]: In 0.5 and before, gladiators were basically interchangeable. They looked a bit different and had different perks, but they weren't really unique. That changes in 0.6! Each gladiator now has three stats, Power, Constitution, and Agility, which roughly correspond to damage, health, and chance to hit an dodge. This gives some compelling reasons to pick one gladiator over another as well as to specialize them towards one or another weapon or defensive skill (dodge or block).
[*] [b]Training[/b]: Each week that a gladiator is uninjured and not participating in a match, the gladiator will train to improve the aforementioned stats. Under the hood, the gladiator has a certain proclivity for each stat which will affect their training rate. They also have an overall level of talent which will help them learn stats across the board. These talents and proclivities also affect the initial skill you'll see when you recruit the gladiator.
[*] [b]Aging[/b]: I'm feeling this one in AD 2024 and the gladiators are too. As gladiators get older they heal more slowly and have a significantly harder time keeping up their stats, even if they train regularly. This puts a soft expiration on even the best gladiators and also makes a more interesting choice for recruiting. Obviously, aging (and training) is a somewhat slow process, so I expect the impact of this mechanic to be more apparent as the game expands
[*] [b]Starting Recruits[/b]: To get off to a bit of a quicker start, your roster will now include three gladiators: Dacius - towards the end of his career but quite skilled, Leander - a decent mid-career gladiator, and Pio - a promising youngster. That should give a decent and fairly balanced 'quickstart' to the game.
[/list]

[h2]Minor Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] There are now notifications to let you know when equipment returns to your inventory, when gladiators level up, and when gladiators heal fully. These should help some confusion in which players thought that when a gladiator died, their equipment disappeared with them
[*] Candidates now appear naked and sans-perks to make comparison amongst them easier and to remove the premium you'd pay for their equipment. Since the candidates have no equipment, the equipment display in recruiting has been replaced by a quick-reference on their stats.
[*] Selling a gladiator now automatically unequips all their gear and sends it to the inventory
[*] Added help indicators and tooltips to several menus to better explain their function
[*] New tooltips, though mostly affecting all the new UI added for stats
[*] Changed the basic unit of time from a day to a week to make a little more sense with the rate of training and injuries, as well as how a gladiator ages
[*] Bugfix: prevent a gladiator who fought this week from also healing the same week
[*] Bugfix: previously, you could accept a challenge, then pass a week or more, then start the challenge.  That is no longer possible and the 'advance time' button change into a button (a skull) to start match since that's what it seemed like it should be doing anyhow
[*] Bugfix: The perk icons no longer overlap text on the detailed gladiator stat tooltip
[/list]

[h1]What's Next[/h1]
The holidays!

...

I haven't quite decided on the theme of [i]next[/i] major patch yet, but in the next [i]few[/i] patches I hope to:
- Spice up the combat visuals and sound effects
- Introduce visiting characters who come with special events
- Find out more about what's happening at your school out of combat. Who trains your gladiators? What do they eat? Where do they live? What are they thinking?

Got opinions, let me know! I just found out about the discussions tab on Steam, so I'll start to look there for feedback. And if you want to get an inside scoop on new updates, join the mailing list at the bottom of https://vittoriagames.com.


Until next time,
Nick

notes.title: Update 0.5.1 - Balance & Bugfixes
notes.content:
Salve, readers! Patch 0.5.0 introduced practice matches and healing and I didn't get the new balance quite right. With a thank you to Malthe Sørensen, who contacted me by email with some detailed notes on where the balance felt off. Thanks to that and some further playtesting of my own, this patch fixes a couple small bugs and tweaks some values to keep the demo challenging, but eminently possible to win.

[h2]Changes [/h2]
[h3]Features[/h3]
- Added a UI element to show what level gladiators are when recruiting them

[h3]Balance Changes[/h3]
- Increased daily healing rate from 6 to 10 . This is a pretty dramatic increase that should get your gladiators back into the fight quicker and leave more room to experiment, learn, and earn money between practice matches.
- Increased starting funds from 2500 to 3000
- Slightly increased "wood axe" damage and cost. Slightly increased mitigation from the high-tier "plate" armors


[h3]Bugfixes[/h3]
- Fixed bug in which no gladiators would not heal on days where the player opted for a practice match
- Fixed a bug where buying or selling a gladiator would not refresh the schedule to show or hide the 'fully recovered' event
- Fixed a bug where the demo ended on the practice match after the last scheduled match

notes.title: Update 0.5.0 - Healing, Exhibition Matches, and Time
notes.content:
Salve, dear readers! It's the end of June and time for a major update before I head off on vacation for a couple weeks. So...

[h2]What's New in 0.5.0[/h2]
[h3]Major Features[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Healing:[/b] Gladiators wounded in combat will now remain wounded after the exit the arena. Each day (more on that in a second) they will heal a small fixed amount of health. You can, of course, return them to the arena should you be in a foolhardy mood.
[*] [b]Exhibition Matches:[/b] Before all matches were fatal and you had fight matches continuously to advance. That made it difficult to feel like you were progressing your gladiators and getting to know them. As of this update, you only need fight the major, preset 'sponsored' matches. However, to have a chance to beat those, you will need to judiciously participate in optional, non-lethal exhibition matches (at most one a day) to make the money and gain the experience you need to stand up to the sponsored matches.
[*] [b]Time for Time:[/b] To underpin healing, exhibition matches, and - soon - training, Forum Mortuorum needed a real concept of time. This update adds it along with a new schedule UI.
[/list]
[h3]Minor Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added some new tooltips to buttons that have only icons displayed
[*] Added a 'shine' effect to some buttons to help orient and remind you what actions you likely need to take
[*] Expanded the 'navigation bar menu' to include buttons for the upcoming training and school upgrade pages
[*] Changed the cursor graphic on the Main Menu and added fade-in/out when starting the game.
[*] Rebalanced match sizes, difficulty, and starting denarii to adapt to the various new changes, and to make the difficulty curve more intuitive
[/list]

[h2]What's Next?[/h2]
Next (major) update (0.6.X) will be focused on making gladiators uniquely skilled (right now they're all blandly similar) as well as a bit quirky.  Additionally, it will introduce the ability to train them (while they're healthy) to further develop their talents.

That's all for now. See you next patch!
Nick

notes.title: Patch 0.4.3 - More SFX & Bugfixes
notes.content:
Just tidying up before moving onto bigger better patches. Patch 0.4.3 updates the demo with the following:

[h3]SFX[/h3]
- Changes 'hit' SFX to reflect which weapon is hitting. Now, only punches go 'thwack'
- Added sound effects to perks, equipping equipment, selling equipment by dragging, the menu open button, dialog boxes, and alert 'toasts'

[h3]Graphics[/h3]
- Caps framerate to the screen refresh rate to avoid working the GPU hard for no reason (which also causes some GPUs to whine)

[h3]Bugfixes[/h3]
- Fixed a bug where buying and selling a couple of gladiators would cause one of them to be dismissed from the recruiting pool.
- Fixed a bug where all gladiators with the same facial features would inadvertently also share the same skin tone
- Fixed a typo that caused the 'Exit to Desktop' menu button to read 'Exit to Menu'
- Fixed a bug where the tooltip for perks was floating off to the left of the screen
- Fixed bug where the 'start match' sound played even if you were unable to start the match due to having no selected gladiators

notes.title: Patch 0.4.2
notes.content:
Hi there! Welcome to the inaugural patch notes for Forum Mortuorum!

[h2]What's New in 0.4.2?[/h2]
[h3]Features[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Sound Effects:[/b] for combat & most UI buttons
[*] [b]Audio Settings:[/b] in case you don't like my sound effects :'(
[*] Improved main menu background graphics (sharpness, color choice, & scaling). Enjoy some pleasant blues for a change
[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where gladiators would occasionally be equipped with both a 2-handed weapon and an off-hand item
[*] Fixed visual bugs on the gladiator stats panel in which text would sometimes overlap
[*] Eliminated UI 'flashing' on stats panel when rapidly hovering over gladiators in quick succession
[/list]

[h2]What's Next?[/h2]
Next (major) update (0.5.X) will be all about progressing your gladiator's skills and keeping them alive! Here's what's in the works:

[olist]
[*] [b]Gladiator training, injuries, and healing:[/b] When a gladiator fights to the death or near death, it's going to take them time to bounce back from their injuries. While they heal you [i]should[/i] keep them out of fights. For this reason, it's going to start being a good idea to keep a larger team of gladiators between fights! Healthy, idle gladiators will train each day to improve their skills, rewarding you for maturing your recruits before putting them into a real match.
[*][b]Non-lethal exhibition matches:[/b] While it's important to experiment and gain experience from 'practice' matches, it's frustrating that right now they're just as lethal as challenge matches. Next patch will replace these with (mostly) non-lethal exhibition matches where your gladiators can gain some experience while surrendering well before they take lethal damage.
[*] [b]Better challenge selection:[/b] Right now, challenge selection is confusing. Why would a fight against 5 gladiators be easier than a fight against say, 3? The answer comes down to equipment and perks, but the current challenge selection doesn't tell you that. So, the next (major) patch will overhaul this UI to give you more information about who you'll face!
[/olist]

[h2]In case you missed it...[/h2]
Since I haven't published patch notes before, it's likely you missed the [b]MAJOR[/b] 0.4.0 update in February. That headliner of that patch was the introduction of a real inventory, shopping, and equipping system and a major overhaul of the school UI including a much requested readout of gladiator stats. It also greatly expanded the available weapons and armor (and their balance), completely overhauled the AI to make combat more fluid. It's kind of a big deal and if you even slightly enjoyed Forum Mortuorum before February, it's worth giving it another shot now.
